speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether LTA has investigated the root causes of the incidents of bus fires involving Mercedes-Benz Citaro buses in 2026; (b) whether additional safety protocols and mechanical audits are being implemented across older public transport fleet assets to ensure passenger safety; and (c) if so, what are they.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: No one was injured in the incidents, but every such fire is an incident too many.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: On his first query as to whether LTA has investigated, the answer is yes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: First, I would like to ask what fire detection or suppression systems are currently installed in the engine compartments of such public buses and whether LTA is reviewing the need for enhanced thermal monitoring or fire detection systems on especially the older buses to provide earlier warning of potential fires?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My next supplementary question; whether maintenance audit requirements and fault reporting standards are applied consistently across all public transport operators (PTOs)?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I believe that the buses are used by different operators.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And what measures LTA takes to verify compliance and identify any gaps in maintenance practices?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It is, in a sense, related to the cause of each respective fires.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, the systems in place really depends on the cause that resulted in the fire.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I would say that as far as the buses' electrical systems are concerned, there are indicators which will indicate the start of a fire and the bus captains would have to take the necessary steps if the bus is being used.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Of course, beyond that, we have the maintenance regimes and each manufacturer would indicate the service length or time for each parts that is being used.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Moving on to the maintenance regime of these buses, indeed, the Citaro buses would have a certain manual that has to be complied with and LTA's expectation would be that the manual for the maintenance must be followed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On the third point about audits, I would say that for the three cases, LTA has not just been in contact with the PTOs, but has also been in contact with the manufacturer – in this case, Mercedes-Benz.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They have also come in to check the systems and they have found no abnormalities which may have a system-wide impact.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We are continuing to monitor the situation and will not hesitate to take any further steps necessary to maintain passenger safety.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Actually, my first supplementary question was asking about what fire detection or suppression systems are currently installed in the engine compartments and whether LTA is reviewing the enhanced thermal monitoring or fire detection system on the buses – not just the cause of the problem.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I am obliged to the hon Member for his clarification.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I can confirm that there are fire suppression systems available for the engine compartment.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But as to the specifics, I do not have the details at this point in time.
